doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

chapter: Black Radio and the new waves
title: Working with unknown artists
summary: He first had to establish himself with known names and now wants to make an album with underground artists.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Do you work with a lot of unknowns?

No. Not at the moment. I presently have a lot of friends that are unknown artists that are dope. I know a lot of great artists that are quote unknown. But I even tell them, from the beginning, people are like, “why don’t you have me on.” And I’m like, “let me put myself in a position first so that I can bring you all up.” And people have to understand that I have to put myself in the position and I have to use people who are already established in order to do that. You know what I mean? So now I’m in a position, I can do that. I can bring some people who no one knows, but now I have clout and people listen to what I think. You know? So if I say this person is dope, a lot of people are going to be like, “they must be dope.” You know? But if I woulda did that from the beginning man it wouldn’t be me or you. You know we ain’t helping each other out. So you know, so eventually I wanna do an album with a bunch of underground artists that no one knows that people should know. I’m definitely going to do that record too you know.
